claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 is a phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy system.
This alloy forms a complex crystalline microstructure under slow cooling.
Melt-spinning can impose cooling rates of approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s on this alloy.
Ultra-rapid quenching improves glass-forming ability relative to cooling at approximately 52 or 3018 K/s.
Ultra-rapid quenching yields a higher amorphous-phase fraction than slower cooling.
Ultra-rapid quenching increases the crystallization onset temperature of the resulting amorphous material.
Ultra-rapid quenching improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
A cooling rate on the order of at least 10^5 K/s is the critical threshold for the proposed effect.
Cooling rates significantly below 10^5 K/s may fail to produce the proposed improvement.
The intervention must be conducted under an inert atmosphere and controlled melt conditions.
Increasing cooling rate produces enhanced undercooling in this alloy.
Enhanced undercooling suppresses atomic diffusion and nucleation.
Ultra-rapid cooling leaves insufficient time for atoms to rearrange into crystalline phases.
Phosphorus disrupts crystalline nucleation in the alloy.
Phosphorus addition and high mixing entropy enhance the alloy's glass-forming ability.
Rapid cooling and phosphorus jointly lock in a stable amorphous configuration that withstands subsequent thermal perturbations.
Ultra-rapid quenching produces a more homogeneous amorphous structure with reduced microstructural heterogeneity.
The intervention should also work in phosphorus-containing alloys compositionally related to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Changing phosphorus content or the other constituent elements may alter the critical cooling rate and improvement magnitude.

contradictions.description: The design states that samples will be subjected to three different cooling conditions, but explicitly describes only two condition categories: slow cooling over a broad 50–3000 K/s range and ultra-rapid melt-spinning at 10^5–10^6 K/s. The approximately 52 K/s and 3018 K/s conditions should be specified separately if three groups are intended.
